text:
**Short answer: about 200-400 W of solar.** The right size depends on how fast you want it to refill.

**The math** (the sources use slightly different assumptions)
- Daily energy = panel watts × peak sun hours × about 0.70-0.75 for real-world losses ([Watt48](https://www.watt48.com/guides/solar-panel-charging-power-station), [Enough Watts](https://enoughwatts.com/guides/how-much-solar-to-recharge)).
- **200 W panel:** about 630 Wh/day at 4.5 peak sun hours, so roughly 1.5 days for a full recharge ([Power Preflight](https://powerpreflight.com/guides/solar-panel-sizing-portable-power-stations/)).
- **One-day recharge:** about 340 W at 4 sun hours, 270 W at 5, and 230 W at 6 ([Power Runtime](https://power-runtime.pages.dev/guides/solar-charging/)). In a good summer that's about 300 W, and in a northern winter about 700 W or more ([Held in Reserve](https://www.heldinreserve.com/power/solar-panels-recharge-power-station/)).
- **Rule of thumb:** battery Wh ÷ 5 gives about 200 W for a day and a half of decent sun.

**Before you buy**
- Check your station's maximum solar input watts. Panels beyond that limit add nothing.
- Check its input voltage window. Panels wired in series add voltage, and exceeding the limit can damage the station. Parallel wiring is the safer default.
- Check the connector type (MC4, XT60, DC barrel), and get the adapter cable if needed.
- If you run loads while charging, the net recharge is slower.

Dealectric says it tested the code in the brand's cart on 2026-10-25. At 400 W, this could refill in about a day in good sun, if the P1800's solar input limit allows 400 W. The search results don't list that spec, so check it first.
- [BLUETTI AC180 + 200 W solar kit](https://dealectric.com/go/bluetti-ac180-200w-solar-kit) (1,152 Wh): $769, or $730.55 with code AFF5OFF. This is the 200 W, about 1.5-day option.
- If you already own a 1,000 Wh station, the [ALLPOWERS SP037 400 W foldable panel](https://dealectric.com/go/allpowers-sp037-400w-solar-panel) is $299, or $269.10 with ALLPOWERS26. Confirm your station's input limits first.
